bullets.title: Fed hike today near-certain; markets pricing 25bp with >90% probability
bullets.body: FOMC expected to raise rates 25bp today, with 92bps cumulative tightening priced in (3-4 hikes). Historical precedent shows Fed has never defied market consensus when hike is priced above 90%. JPM base case: 25bp with no guidance = S&P +0.25%-0.75%; a hold would be bearish and trigger inflation concerns. 83% of JPM macro conference attendees expect a hike before year-end.

bullets.title: Retail sales crushed expectations; Q3 GDP tracking above 2%
bullets.body: August headline retail sales +1.2% m/m (vs. 0.8% consensus), control group +1.4% (vs. 0.5%). Morgan Stanley raised 3Q GDP tracking to 2.4% and real consumption to 2.9% annualized. Real PCE tracking 3.2% annualized for Q3 per one macro shop, well above Bloomberg consensus of 2.1%. Strength was broad-based: e-commerce +2.6%, restaurants +1.2%, sporting goods +1.2%; building materials the lone soft spot.

bullets.title: Hedgeye inflation nowcast rises to 3.61% y/y; short bonds remains core position
bullets.body: Hedgeye raised its September CPI nowcast +21bp to 3.61% y/y (up +7bp from the Sept 11 publication), flipping from sideways to moderate inflationary bias. Their model targets UST 2yr at 4.75% and 10yr at 5.09%, with the strategy to short bonds on bounces and short bond proxies (utilities). Inflation expected to accelerate into Q4 before falling sharply by mid-2027, with risk that Fed tightens into a slowdown.

bullets.title: 10-year yield approaching 5%; equity-breaking threshold now seen at 5.5-6%
bullets.body: Bond yields breaking out: UST 2yr to 4.75%, 10yr to 5.09%, 30yr to 5.43% per Hedgeye. JPMorgan macro conference participants argued the equity-breaking threshold for 10Y Treasuries may be 5.5-6.0%, not the previously feared 5% level, as higher rate-insensitive sectors (AI, healthcare, services) now dominate growth. Term premium has risen to ~125bps driven primarily by fiscal concerns. 60% of JPM conference attendees see 10Y ending above 4.75%.

bullets.title: S&P 500 range 7,521-7,747; Wells Fargo cuts year-end target to 7,700
bullets.body: Wells Fargo lowered its S&P 500 year-end target to 7,700 from 7,950, citing valuation compression and stretched positioning — equity allocations at ~72% vs fair value of 60%, the widest gap since 1969. Goldman estimates $19.5B in global CTA selling risk if markets stay weak, with 7,500 as critical support. S&P futures +0.23-0.4% pre-market; VIX at 16.71 (+2.9%) with Hedgeye's signal level at 16.55.

bullets.title: AI capex cycle intact and rate-insensitive; hyperscalers outperforming semis by ~37% QTD
bullets.body: Multiple conference takeaways (JPM, MS, Citi) converge: no signs of meaningful capex demand slowdown despite monetization concerns and pacing headlines. Hyperscaler basket up +9% QTD vs semis basket down -28% QTD. AI safety and alignment efforts require MORE compute, not less. Consensus AI capex now ~$900bn by year-end (+85% YoY); hyperscaler net debt/equity at ~13% with sufficient capacity for 2-year capex growth. Nvidia GPU rental pricing now $16/hour vs $5 a year ago.

bullets.title: Compute futures launching by year-end; ICE/Nodal targeting early October
bullets.body: Cash-settled compute futures based on Nvidia Hopper (H100) or Blackwell (B200/B300) chips expected from ICE and Nodal via self-certification in early October; CME following after CFTC comment period closes October 20. Futures will enable risk management for neoclouds, debt investors, and compute buyers — a structural market development for AI infrastructure financing.

bullets.title: Hedgeye ETF re-rank: adding IBIT, IGV, COLO, EWZ; selling OIH
bullets.body: Keith McCullough added IBIT (+13 spots 1-week), IGV (+9 spots), COLO (+11 spots), EWZ (+19 spots 1-month), and XLE/ETHA at minimum allocation; sold all FXC and trimmed OIH. Bitcoin and software (IGV) leading re-rank, with Brazil equities (EWZ) also flagged as offering asymmetric upside if Lula re-election odds (~47%) continue to fall.

bullets.title: Consumer credit quality at multi-decade lows (in a good way); spending tracking 6-10% growth
bullets.body: August credit card delinquency rates improved 33bps y/y and NCO rates improved 42bps y/y. Visa US business grew 10% last quarter. Consumer topline spending growing 6-10% with credit quality at or near multi-decade lows. Consumer net worth hit record high in Q2 (+$9T), supporting high-end spending; K-shaped consumer narrative increasingly stale as lower-income cohorts accelerate.

bullets.title: UK CPI jumps to 3.1%; BoE expected to hike to 4+ hikes through summer 2027
bullets.body: August UK headline CPI rose 0.5% m/m to 3.1% y/y; core and services CPIs remain sticky at 2.6% and 3.4%. PSC forecasts inflation hitting 4.8% y/y by early 2027, well above 3.3% consensus, as household energy bills could jump ~25% in January. Gilt yields at 19-year highs; BoE expected to begin hiking no later than November with 4 total moves. UK growth tepid at 1.0-1.2% handle through 2027.

bullets.title: NAHB housing index falls to 32, lowest in a year; mortgage applications down 10% YoY
bullets.body: September NAHB Housing Market Index dropped 3 points to 32, with current conditions -4 to 35 and sales expectations -6 to 37. 38% of builders cut prices (up from 35% in August); labor shortages worsened by immigration enforcement. MBA purchase data down 10% YoY, refinances down 61% YoY as 10-year pushes 5% and mortgage rates near 7%.

bullets.title: US midterms: Dems 86% to take House; energy prices +16.5% on Iran-Houthi escalation
bullets.body: Betting markets show 86% probability Democrats take the House, 48% GOP holds the Senate. Most likely Dem Senate flips: NC (92%), Maine (67%), Alaska (66%). Energy prices surged from $91 to $106/bbl (+16.5%) on Iran-Houthis conflict, Strait of Hormuz risk (~8mm bpd oil, ~4bcf/d LNG). Top voter issues: economy, affordability, Iran conflict; data center/AI regulation emerging in Michigan and Texas.

bullets.title: Freight costs up 162% YoY; trucking constrained by regulation and immigration enforcement
bullets.body: Shanghai Containerized Freight Index costs up 162% YoY, accelerating sequentially. Cass Truckload Linehaul Index up 11.3% YoY in August. Trucking capacity constrained by regulatory pressures and federal immigration enforcement. JBHT down 10% on profit warning citing higher costs; NSC cited a 250bp fuel headwind to Q3 operating ratio.

bullets.title: UBS Q4 strategy: AI broadens beyond hyperscalers; favor large-cap growth and industrials
bullets.body: UBS sees AI leadership broadening to industrials, healthcare, utilities, and financials beyond the original hyperscaler/chip cohort. Large-cap growth and industrials favored over consumer discretionary and small caps. Equity, credit, and FX volatility seen as underpriced given elevated geopolitical, energy, and bond risks. Policy easing expected to arrive sooner than markets expect from 2027 onwards; gold preferred hedge with investor allocations still low.

bullets.title: Retail investor basket down to -3% YTD from +22% peak; tech valuations compressed
bullets.body: S&P 500 IT sector trading at 20.5x forward earnings vs 10-year average of 23x; Mag 7 approaching technical breakout. Retail investor basket down to -3% YTD from +22% peak on May 28, with high retail sentiment basket down 2% yesterday. 3-month momentum +5% vs 12-month -6.7%, largest relative underperformance in 5 years. Goldman estimates $19.5B in CTA selling risk if markets stay weak.

bullets.title: AI capex private credit boom: $600B AI corporate borrowing in 2026; KKR warning on 'tourists'
bullets.body: AI-related corporate borrowing reached ~$600B in 2026, roughly 4% of total corporate debt stock. KKR doing $80B private IG YTD (+104% vs full year prior); Apollo 200+ deals at ~$150bn high grade capital. But KKR running 4-5% defaults for 3yr; direct lending defaults + non-accruals up to 6.5% from 5.0% at YE25. KKR warning on 'tourists' underwriting data centers and supplier-customer circularity in chip financing.

bullets.title: AMZN Project Mercury: 10x same-day fulfillment to 1,000+ facilities by 2031
bullets.body: Amazon Project Mercury targets expansion from ~85 to 1,000+ same-day fulfillment centers by 2031 with $6.8B capex spend in 2026-27, putting hubs within 10 miles of most US Prime customers. Same-day customers add 3x more items to baskets and spend 80%+ more. Projected to reach 50% of fulfilled volume by 2035 vs ~28% by 2029. CART fell -4.1% pre-market on the news.

bullets.title: OpenAI in $1.2T valuation funding talks; Anthropic moving toward IPO
bullets.body: OpenAI in early talks for a private funding round at approximately $1.2T valuation. Anthropic moving forward with IPO amid capital questions. SoftBank CDS hit a three-year high on delayed OpenAI monetization and $64.6B investment exposure. OpenAI users spent more on OpenAI models than Anthropic last week for the first time in over two years; ChatGPT fastest-growing among top 10 websites in August.

bullets.title: Chip supply tightness persists; AMD targeting 50%+ server CPU share; AMAT flagging 8 quarters visibility
bullets.body: Demand expected to materially outstrip chip supply for some time, with supply access a key differentiator. AMD targeting 50%+ CPU server share in a $200B+ TAM (implying $100B+ business); Venice launch on 2nm benefits from TSMC available capacity. AMAT citing 8 quarters of unprecedented visibility. JPM most positive on semi equipment (supply bottlenecks shifting to tools) and advanced packaging; cautious on memory.

bullets.title: GEV electrification backlog $40B+; utility demand driving 62% of orders, data centers 38%
bullets.body: Bernstein reiterated buy on GEV, viewing it as a durable electrification play beyond data centers. Electrification equipment backlog exceeds $40B in Q2, representing ~3 years of revenues. Data center orders were $5B in H1 (38% of electrification orders); utility-driven demand accounts for 62%. GEV raised its 2030 capacity target from 24GW to 30GW at the Morgan Stanley conference.
